properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 29 at 1:44AM PDT until October 30 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 1 PM PDT today. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 1 PM today to 2 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal residents and managers of
infrastructure in the warned/advisory area should prepare for
rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property. Highest tides will occur around 11 AM today and noon
on Friday. Observed high tides are 1.4 to 1.6 feet above
astronomical tide predictions.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 29 at 1:25AM MST until October 30 at 10:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall over saturated
soils and waterways that flooded as recently as last week.

* WHERE...Yavapai County and northern Gila County.

* WHEN...From 10 AM MST Friday morning through 10 PM MST Friday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Another round of tropical moisture arrives in central Arizona
Friday morning. Expect generalized accumulations of 0.50" to
1.00" of rainfall within the watch area, locally higher amounts
of up to 2.00" possible in thunderstorms.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 29 at 4:20AM EDT until October 29 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Thursday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Ocean overwash impacts will continue through today,
especially around high tide in areas where dunes have been
compromised. NC-12 between the Basnight Bridge and Rodanthe
remains closed. The next high tide is around 10 PM tonight and
around 10:15 AM Thursday. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will remain high with a King
Tide Cycle in place through today. The morning high tide will
be the highest of the two daily tides.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 29 at 1:05AM MST until October 30 at 10:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Arizona, including the following
areas, Dripping Springs, Globe/Miami, Mazatzal Mountains,
Pinal/Superstition Mountains, San Carlos, Southeast Gila County,
Superior and Tonto Basin.

* WHEN...From Friday afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Abundant moisture over the area will combine with an incoming
weather system to provide for showers and thunderstorms on
Friday, some of which are expected to produce moderate to heavy
rainfall. Any strong thunderstorms will have the potential to
produce rainfall rates as high as 1-2 inches per hour. Localized
rainfall amounts of one to two inches are expected within the
Watch area on Friday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.instruction:

be hazardous to small craft in the vicinity of the Columbia River
Bar. Mariners are advised to obtain the latest bar conditions
from the United States Coast Guard before attempting to cross the
bar.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 29 at 3:54AM EDT until October 29 at 12:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected and strong north to south longshore current. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot of inundation above
ground level expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and
tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal New Hanover County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through this evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 9 AM this morning to noon
EDT today.

* IMPACTS...Low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal
Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks may observe minor coastal
flooding. Check with local officials for any road closures or
impacts. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 29 at 2:52AM CDT until October 30 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest and the Panhandle of Texas, including
the following counties, in northwest Texas, Bailey, Childress,
Cochran, Cottle, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hockley,
Kent, King, Lamb, Lubbock, Lynn, Motley, Stonewall, Terry and
Yoakum. In the Panhandle of Texas, Briscoe, Castro, Hall, Parmer
and Swisher.

* WHEN...From this afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread rain showers are expected to develop Thursday
afternoon and persist through much of Friday. Showers may be
heavy at times, especially late Thursday into early Friday
morning, and may result in flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
